name: Speculation Rules prefetch and prerender
plain: A page can load a likely next page early, so a site may see a request before the person visits.
meaning: Prefetch or prerender makes the destination server log a hit, and run scripts, before any click, sending Sec-Purpose: prefetch;prerender. Analytics can over count; cookies from a prefetched response apply only on activation.

access.persistence: Prefetch cache about 5 minutes in Chrome
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

safari.note: Not supported at time of research, verify

limits.headline: Can load a likely next page early, so a site may see a visit first
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when a page guesses where you will go next
can: Load a likely next page before you click
Show the next page almost instantly when you click
Let the next site see a request before you visit
cannot: Run when Chrome's data saver is on or the connection is poor
Show you the page until you click, or count it as a visit in some tools
Load pages from a different site without extra signals
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet support it. Firefox and Safari do not.

story.what_it_is: A page can load a likely next page early, so a site may see a visit before you click.

marketing.name: Prerender pages
marketing.pitch: Chrome says speculation rules can load pages ahead of time so the next click feels instant.

story.for_you: You click a link and the next page appears almost at once. Behind the scenes, the browser loaded it before you clicked. The site may log a hit even if you never open it.
story.for_makers: Instant page loads raise sales and reading time. But prefetching makes the server count a visit early and can run scripts before you arrive. Analytics must wait for activation to avoid inflated numbers.

use_cases.example: A shop prerenders the product page you are likely to open, so checkout feels fast.
A news site prefetches the next article so it opens instantly.
A game portal prefetches the page of the game you hover over, so it loads in a blink.
A tool must ignore hits from prefetched pages, or visit counts go up.
An ad system waits for activation before it counts an impression.
A search result page prerenders the top result so it opens at once.

risks: Server sees visits you never made

technical_bounds: Same-site prefetch carries cookies; cross-origin uses an isolated session without them
Not done when Data Saver or Save-Data is on, or in low memory
Chrome limits concurrent prefetch and prerender counts

abuse: Phantom page views, privacy leak of intent before click

history.change: Prerender2 shipped for omnibox and speculation rules
